evidence_required: FT-001-AC-002 RED: same-scope sequential or concurrent candidates can create more than one admitted identity or retain the losing object; GREEN: PostgreSQL uniqueness returns exactly one accepted and one duplicate, deletes only the losing candidate and leaves Photo/pending/downstream counts unchanged beyond the winner; decisive comparison: before/after database and object inventories contain one admitted pair and one retained original; artifact: concurrent integration output and count projection.
purpose: Complete the database-arbitrated duplicate branch without merging it back into atomic publication or crash recovery.
success_outcome: Sequential and concurrent same-СПА/date/checksum candidates yield one accepted Photo, visible duplicate outcomes and deletion of each losing candidate without extra state.
anti_goals: Do not change the atomic success transaction, own crash-window recovery, or add client-side deduplication.
Do not expose the existing Photo/object identity or create Batch/idempotency infrastructure.

stop_conditions: Database uniqueness cannot be the sole concurrent arbitration authority.
Cleanup would delete the winner or any object not owned by the losing request.
The task would require a lock service, queue or distributed coordination.

constraints: PostgreSQL uniqueness on spa_id, visit_date and checksum_sha256 decides the winner.
A duplicate exposes no existing photo_id or object identity.
Candidate deletion is idempotent and scoped only to the losing request key.
invariants: A duplicate creates no Photo, pending state, searchable result, teaser candidate or contribution to N.
Concurrent same-scope attempts admit exactly one winner.
The winner retains its original opaque object and the loser deletes only its candidate.
verification_targets: Sequential and concurrent disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO probes compare exact winner/loser outcomes and owned cleanup.
